neighbours.label: 'not' or 'for' that marks a counterfactual condition (had it not been for, if it weren't for, had not, but for, were it not for)
fire: The town would have flooded had it not been for the new wall.
If it weren't for the rain, we would have reached the summit.
He would have drowned had not a fisherman pulled him out.
Were it not for the map, the hikers would have been lost.
The team might have won if it hadn't been for the injury.
We would have missed the train had the taxi not arrived early.
If it was not for my sister, I would never have learned to swim.
The crops would have failed if the river had not risen in spring.
quiet: The town built a new wall after the flood last year.
We waited for the rain to stop before we reached the summit.
He had not seen a fisherman on the lake all week.
The hikers did not bring a map, so they asked for directions.
The team played for an hour before the injury.
The taxi was not early, so we ran for the train.
My sister is not a strong swimmer, but she tries.
The river had not risen by the end of spring.

notes: Probe: had not our mast 1.03, had it not been for 0.90, if it wasn't for 0.80, were it not for 0.65, if ... had not been 0.62, but for 0.47; plain 'had not seen', 'waited for', 'did not' all <0.02.
